newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanians seek fair trial for soldier gunman.
newsitem.headline: Jordanians seek fair trial for soldier gunman.

text.p: Jordan's powerful unions and opposition deputies launched a campaign on Sunday to ensure a fair trial for a Jordanian soldier who gunned down seven Israeli teenagers.

"It is only natural the union of lawyers should demand that a fair trial be held for the soldier with all the guarantees of justice," Hussein Majli, head of Jordan's Lawyers Association, told Reuters.

Majli also said that a meeting on Sunday decided to launch a broad-based campaign to ensure the soldier, army driver Segeant Ahmed Mousa Mustafa al-Daqamsa, who shot dead the girls on Thursday, would have an fair and public trial.

The campaigners, who include professional unions and opposition deputies along with Laith Shubailat who heads the Engineers Union and is a leading critic of the government, said in a statement the soldier was "innocent until proven guilty."
Majli said the meeting had asked the lawyers' union to form a defence team, to insist that it be present during Daqamsa's interrogation by a military tribunal, and to defend him in court.
King Hussein, who has condemned the shooting as a "vile crime", has appointed veteran security official Mohammed Kailani to head investigations into the soldier's motives.

In apparent sympathy with the soldier, the comittee said Israel continued to occupy Arab land, confiscate Palestinian territory and evict its inhabitants, accusing the Jewish state of "killing and torturing hundred of thousands of men, women and elderly since its creation in 1948."

Referring to King Hussein's conciliatory visit to Israel on Sunday to pay condolences to the families of the girls, the campaigners said "the shooting should be considered in its natural framework and without blowing it out of proportion."
Some Jordanians privately criticised the king's visit as a excessive display which they fear Israel is exploiting to defuse Arab anger at Jewish settlement building.
The campaigners also said the site of the shooting in north Jordan's Baqoura area, which was leased to Israeli farmers under their 1994 peace treaty, was "still under occuption".
The leasing of the area, located south of Israel's Sea of Galilee, upset many Jordanians who saw it as perpetuating the presence of a former enemy on their territory.

The campaigners, apparantly reacting to the king's visit to Israel, decided to send their own delegation on Monday to pay respects to the family of the soldier in the small village of Ibdr in north Jordan.
The family is a tribe from Jordan's East Bank, whose tribes form the bedrock of King Hussein's army.
